key: I seek for no release, no turning back therefrom. May he who knows the way, the Leader, guide me straight.
s: Opening a hymn to all the gods, the singer pictures himself yoked like a willing horse to a load; Sāyaṇa, on 5.46.1, takes the load as the sacrifice and the guide as the god who rules within, going before along its paths.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.46.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 199507 (2019)

evidence.words: “धुरि यज्ञात्मिकायाम् “अयुजि युक्तोऽभवत् … “विद्वान् मार्गाभिज्ञोऽन्तर्यामी देवः “पुरएता पुरतो गन्ता सन् "पथः यज्ञमार्गान् “ऋजु अकुटिलं “नेषति प्रापयति
evidence.gloss: To the pole that consists of sacrifice he was yoked … The knowing one, knower of the way, the god who rules within (antaryāmin), going before, leads along the paths, the paths of sacrifice, straight, without crookedness.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 5.46.1, at [399,1]), two whole sentences from the end of 5.46.1. Plain sense faithful: the hymn is to the Viśvedevas (5.46.2 to 5.46.8 invoke the gods and their wives), and 5.46.1 has the singer yoked horselike to the pole; the clause repeats no four-word run of the key. Sāyaṇa glosses dhuri as yajñātmikāyām (the pole is the sacrifice) and vidvān … puraetā as mārgābhijño ’ntaryāmī devaḥ purato gantā, leading along yajñamārgān (the paths of sacrifice). “Load” renders dhur (Wilson: burthen), so the sentence stays within his words. Entry-check ok.
